coupling: The AtomicWait edit uses a signed i32-to-i64 conversion for memory32 only when the memory uses explicit bounds checks; shared memories still use the trap-handler path and remain clean by themselves. The later shared-memory edit routes shared memories to explicit checks so their bounds observe the dynamically loaded backing-store length. That selection activates the signed conversion for an in-bounds index at 0x80000000: the bounds check accepts the unsigned index, but the wait builtin receives a sign-extended negative offset and performs an invalid read. Reverting either edited change restores the safe zero-extended offset or the trap-handler path, so neither edit triggers the probe independently.
